description: Four-Two-Three (4-2-3) is a Guts-family poker variant. Each player is dealt four cards face-down; players declare in or out simultaneously (e.g. with a coin in fist). The dealer then deals three common cards face up. Players who stayed in form their best five-card poker hand from their four hole cards plus the three board cards; the best hand wins the pot. All who stayed in and lost must match the pot. Game ends when one player stays in alone and wins.

content.text: Four-Two-Three (4-2-3) is a Guts-family poker variant. Each player is dealt four cards face-down; players declare in or out simultaneously (e.g. with a coin in fist). The dealer then deals three common cards face up. Players who stayed in form their best five-card poker hand from their four hole cards plus the three board cards; the best hand wins the pot. All who stayed in and lost must match the pot. Game ends when one player stays in alone and wins.
Variant of Four-Two-Two (4-2-2), contributed by Brian Johnson; differs by dealing three common cards instead of two face-up cards per player.
Two to ten players; Guts-style games typically work best with around five to ten. All agree ante and optional maximum loss per deal before play.
Cards, chips or money for ante and pot, optional coin for simultaneous declare.
Dealer shuffles and deals four cards face-down to each player. After declarations, dealer deals three common cards face up in the center.
